A1.justification: Both PDFs describe La-Proteina. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original protein-generation and motif-scaffolding experiments, structural-quality evaluations, latent-space analyses and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, refolded-motif evaluations, confidence analyses and sampling-temperature experiments.

M1.justification: The conditional VAE, eight-dimensional residue latents, explicit alpha-carbon representation, two-time flow-matching objective, transformer architectures and sampling procedure remain unchanged. Revised training documentation and motif scores do not establish an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: Appendix J.4 adds a UniProt amino-acid frequency reference for evaluation. The AFDB training sources, PDB/AFDB structural references, protein-length coverage and 26 motif tasks remain. The shorter-protein comparisons use lengths already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds Protpardelle-1c to unconditional, structural-quality and indexed all-atom scaffolding comparisons. This substantially strengthens the conditional comparison: Table 3 reports successes on 22 of 26 tasks for the new comparator, whereas the retained Protpardelle baseline solves four. Appendix J.4 also directly compares residue frequencies with ProteinMPNN.

E3.justification: v2 adds motif evaluation against ESMFold-refolded structures, separately reported pLDDT metrics, novelty evaluation using Foldseek 10.941cd33, shorter-length subset evaluations and a 1,000-sample temperature analysis. Appendix C.1 also revises the reported beta-filtered training-set size from approximately 550k to 350k proteins. This reporting revision does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original VAE and sampling-schedule ablations are retained. New analyses test motif preservation after refolding, sensitivity to Foldseek version, comparison fairness for shorter proteins, folding confidence, amino-acid frequency bias and its dependence on sampling temperature (Appendices F.4 and J). These substantially expand the questions examined.

E5.justification: Figure 34 introduces pLDDT distributions with medians, quartiles and 5th/95th percentiles, adding descriptive dispersion and folding-confidence reporting absent from v1. These summarize confidence across generated samples; neither version adds repeated-run uncertainty estimates, seed information or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing motif results change substantially under the same stated 200-sample protocol. In Table 3, unindexed all-atom 6E6R_long changes from 0 total/0 unique successes to 110/83; in Table 4, unindexed tip-atom 5AOU_QUAD changes from 116/92 to 35/29. v2 also adds Protpardelle-1c, pLDDT, refolded-motif, alternative-Foldseek and shorter-protein results. Existing Table 1 scores for retained methods and metrics remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The probabilistic factorization, conditional-independence assumptions, VAE and flow objectives, score expressions and sampling equations are retained in Equations 1–12. No substantive mathematical correction, new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a partially latent framework for joint sequence/full-atom generation, leading generation and scaffolding performance, and scalability to 800 residues. The additional evaluations support these retained claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix J.4 newly interprets amino-acid frequency biases, similarity to ProteinMPNN and the tradeoff between approaching UniProt frequencies and maintaining co-designability at higher temperatures. The monomer-only applicability limitation and the main explanations of latent locality and sampling schedules remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-release link and reproducibility statement, identifies Foldseek versions, and documents Protpardelle-1c checkpoint and sample provenance. It also specifies the existing 390k-step training budget as 300k steps without beta-sheet filtering followed by 90k with filtering. Most architecture, optimizer, hardware and runtime details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lu et al. (2025) on Protpardelle-1c and Didi et al. (2026) on a binder-design extension, while removing the Shanehsazzadeh et al. (2023) and Xu et al. (2023) references. The broader positioning of partially latent protein generation remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the abstract, contribution list, architecture overview and conclusion, and adds ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements plus new appendix subsections. Much of the existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document adopts ICLR typography, margins and headers, with widespread resizing and reflow. Table 1 gains a baseline row and pLDDT column; comparison plots gain Protpardelle-1c; motif displays are reordered; and Tables 5–6 and 11–12 and Figures 33–37 are added. Existing ablation and runtime tables are retained under new numbers.

improvement.justification: The stronger Protpardelle-1c comparison and refolded-motif validation improve support for conditional-design claims. Software-version checks, shorter-protein comparisons, sequence-bias analysis and clearer access and training information strengthen an already extensive evaluation. However, substantial revisions to existing motif counts in Tables 3–4 are unexplained, limiting traceability. The net quality improvement is supported but modest.
